newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, recovers from earlier lows.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, recovers from earlier lows.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mixed after recovering from their earlier lows thanks to spillover support from CBOT soybeans and a lack of follow-through selling, traders said.
"Just like yesterday when we were unable to set off technical buy stops on the rally, today we couldn't set off technical sell stops (due to) light volumes," a trader said.

Short covering of the December contract had driven KCBT wheat higher in recent days. But that short covering appeared to dry up at Tuesday's midsession, pressuring the market and causing the December/March spread to crumble, traders said.
KCBT wheat closed one cent per bushel higher to 3-1/2 cents lower, with Dec down 3-1/2 cents at $4.50. Dec had traded as low as $4.43-1/2, down 10 cents on the day.
The Dec/March spread traded early at 46 cents but narrowed to 38 cents at the midsession before closing at 41 cents.
Traders said it was difficult to read very much into Tuesday's price action because of the light volumes.
CIS bought one million Dec bushels early, but turned seller and sold 500,000 Dec and 500,000 March. CIS and Prudential each bought one million March, traders said. FIMAT sold one million March.
CIS also bull-spread 700,000 Dec/March at 40 to 45 cents.
